repository.note: This remains the pinned discovery baseline. 2026-09-05 findings are an incremental drift audit against current main and the connected Supabase project, not a silent baseline reset.

reference_build.rule: Reference behavior must be read from an explicitly pinned commit. Do not assume the moving branch head equals the original recorded snapshot.

summary: employment_assignments exists and remains the canonical post-hire Work assignment anchor.
work_mode_publications, work_mode_publication_audiences, and work_mode_publication_acknowledgements exist with RLS enabled.
work_mode_check_in_events and work_mode_worker_actions exist with RLS enabled.
staff_shifts, staff_shift_plans, and staff_shift_assignments exist with RLS enabled.
workflow_tasks and workflow_task_assignments exist with RLS enabled.
event_participants does not exist in the audited public schema.
worker_shift_check_in and worker_shift_check_out are stale against the current staff_shifts schema and status constraint.
respond_to_work_assignment remains a reusable assignment-bound RPC.

observations: Work Mode is a transient assignment context on the authenticated general account.
The current hook directly reads employment_assignments in the browser for invited, confirmed, and active assignments.
The current hook tries to augment event scope through event_participants and staff_shifts.
The event_participants query is stale against the audited live schema because public.event_participants does not exist.
The current hook directly reads work_mode_publications and can synthesize publication-only pseudo assignments.
The selected assignment is persisted in sessionStorage and the hook attempts to persist work_mode data to user_sessions.
Assignment accept/decline is sent through /api/work-mode/assignments/[id]/respond.
There is no top-level GET /api/work-mode/assignments server-authorized read-model boundary on current main.
Authorization-sensitive aggregation currently occurs client-side and should be reconciled to the verified reference server-boundary pattern.
Uses authenticated server context and respond_to_work_assignment.
This is the current reusable mutation edge for accept/decline.

work_mode_assignments_collection.required_reconciliation: add a server-authorized GET read model rather than expanding browser aggregation

observations: Defines the current shared hiring/roster/Work concepts but is materially simpler than the verified reference read-model contract.
Shared types should become the sole reusable Work contract rather than keeping parallel hook-local assignment/publication interfaces.
Presents worker applications, engagements, assignments, tours/event access, coordinator chat, tasks, travel, lodging, and attention states.
Worker task actions include acknowledge, start, complete, and block.
Explicitly represents unscheduled and partial-data states.
Uses GET /api/work-mode/assignments as the server-authorized read-model boundary.
Stores a per-user authorized snapshot in sessionStorage for resilient reads.
Revalidates on focus and visibility changes.
Optionally subscribes to targeted employment_assignments, staff_shifts, and work_mode_publications changes.
Supports assignment response and server-confirmed worker actions.
Explicitly avoids offline attendance write replay.

canonical_entities.role: worker shift linkage and schedule source

known_reconciliation_gaps.summary: Current main lacks the server-authorized Work Mode assignments collection/read-model endpoint.
Current Work Mode browser aggregation depends on nonexistent event_participants and must be removed or replaced with verified assignment/tour/event scope.
Current shared Work types are materially simpler than the verified reference read-model contracts and the hook duplicates local interfaces.
Legacy worker_shift_check_in/out RPCs are incompatible with current staff_shifts and must not be used for attendance reconciliation.
Work Hub composition and worker task/attendance integration remain P01 execution tasks, but their backend primitives are now verified rather than assumed missing.
